draft.title: Measuring sleep
card: EEG
An electroencephalograph records electrical activity in the brain, shown as brain waves. Wave patterns show which stage of sleep a person is in.
EMG
An electromyograph records muscle activity. It shows how much muscle tone a person has, which is useful for telling when sleep changes stage.
EOG
An electrooculargraph records eye movements. It shows when the eyes are still and when they move.
Self-report and observation
A sleep diary is the person's own record of when they slept and how they felt. Video monitoring lets an observer see movement, such as rolling over or sleep talking.
draft.remember: EEG is brain, EMG is muscle, EOG is eyes. Diaries give the person's view and video gives an observer's.

a.q: A researcher wants to record when a sleeping person's eyes move. Which measure should the researcher use?
a.why: The EOG records eye movements. The EEG is a tempting choice because it is used in sleep studies, but it records brain waves, not eye movement.
a.clue: Think of what each letter pair records.

b.q: Sam, a Year 12 student in Geelong, says he sleeps badly. A clinic wants a record of his own view of his nights, and also of his body movements seen by a third person. Which pair fits?
b.why: A sleep diary gives Sam's own view and video monitoring gives an observer's view of his movements. The EMG and EEG are tempting, but they record electrical activity with devices, not what a person reports or an observer sees.
b.clue: One source is the person and one is an observer.

problems.detail: 'Electrooculargraph' is misspelt. The correct term, as used in the VCE Study Design, is 'electro-oculograph' (EOG). Students could learn and reproduce the wrong term in exams.
